elements.element: Customer is not subject to any non-compete restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly disclaims any non-compete commitment and broadly permits Customer to develop, acquire, license, sell, or use any product or service. Section 12.4 is framed as permission rather than prohibition.

elements.element: Customer is not subject to any field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 states that nothing restricts Customer from conducting business in any field or territory.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction is limited to one expressly named competing product.
elements.evidence: No non-compete restriction is imposed, so the condition requiring this scope limitation is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction applies only during the agreement term.
elements.evidence: No non-compete restriction is imposed. The 24-month language qualifies an affirmative permission, not a restriction.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction lasts no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: No non-compete restriction is imposed, so there is no restricted period exceeding 12 months.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction excludes Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly permits Customer to develop any product or service, and Section 12.4 also permits development of competing products or services.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction excludes Customer's acquisitions.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly permits Customer to acquire any product or service, and Section 12.4 also permits acquisition of competing products or services.

result.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred position: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction. The fallback is therefore also satisfied because no restriction exists, while development and acquisitions are affirmatively permitted. The change is narrowly directed at reversing the prohibition and does not alter unrelated commercial terms. Drafting quality is reduced because §12.4 unnecessarily retains the term, 24-month, competition, and territory qualifiers around a permission, creating avoidable interpretive ambiguity; deleting §12.4 would be cleaner.
